source.title: Neuron Populations Exhibit Divergent Selectivity with Scale
source.authors: Amil Dravid; Yasaman Bahri; Alexei A. Efros; Yossi Gandelsman

record.file_problem: none; full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures cross-model neuron correspondences and how their number changes with model size, using mutual nearest-neighbour Pearson correlation rather than representational-distance geometry.
record.gate_note: The study directly measures recurring neuron matches across model pairs and their scaling, and measures selectivity of matched and unmatched neuron populations. These findings bear on neuron-level convergence and recurring features, but do not measure similarity between all pairs of inputs or overall representation geometry. The data-filtering case study and document-type specialization analyses are omitted because their outcomes do not measure convergence or recurrence. The quoted neuron-labeling and VLM prompts are experimental prompts, not instructions to an AI reviewing this paper.
record.test_reason: The study measures how many MLP neurons recur across independently trained models of different families, architectures and objectives, and how that count scales with size. It uses mutual nearest-neighbour Pearson matching, not global representational similarity. The results bear on V1, V5, V6 and V7.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors find that the number of recurring (Rosetta) neurons follows a sublinear power law, growing in absolute number but shrinking as a fraction. These neurons become more selective (the 'Neuron Polarization Effect') and more domain-specialized with scale. They explain the scaling with a capacity-allocation superposition model, view Rosetta Neurons as one subset of shared structure measured with proxies, and treat DINOv3 as a failure case showing dependence on the training setup.
record.recipe_differences: Uses mutual nearest-neighbour matching of MLP neuron activations with Pearson correlation and studies the number and selectivity of recurring neurons. It does not measure representational-distance geometry as in the broad Platonic claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The number of matches rises with mutual top-k permissiveness, while fitted exponents remain sublinear. Generated versus real vision inputs yield approximately 93% of the real-image count and roughly 0.8 overlap. Corrupting input alignment removes the scaling trend. The matching-set stability also improves as the number of tokens or images increases.

fits_no_version.finding: With scale, Rosetta Neurons' top activations shift toward code and math documents relative to corpus share in Pythia and Qwen2.5; random non-Rosetta neurons show no such shift (Figs. 7, 29, 30).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Shared cross-model neurons extend to rarer, specialized data domains as models scale.

fits_no_version.finding: A single Pythia-6.9B Rosetta Neuron filters JavaScript at 0.98 F1 versus 0.09 for a non-Rosetta neuron; continued pretraining reaches PPL 3.02 versus oracle 3.01.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Recurring neurons are usable domain selectors (application; not a convergence measure).

record.problems: The study measures neuron matches rather than overall representational-distance geometry. It does not measure model capability/performance as a variable. Selectivity is assessed using modality-specific proxies, including VLM judgments; the authors state that monosemanticity is ambiguous and dependent on evaluation procedure and semantic granularity. Several scaling results are qualitative summaries of plots, and the fraction of neurons matched is not quantified in the text. The main models are existing checkpoints rather than models trained in this study.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted due to the 60-row limit. The document-type specialization and data-filtering results were not included because their reported outcomes do not measure cross-model convergence or recurrence.

untested.parts: Global representational geometry (kernel or kNN alignment over inputs); capability or performance as the scaling variable; cross-modal or cross-objective alignment beyond neuron matching.
Entire version: no vision–language paired comparison.
Entire version: no same-architecture different-seed comparison (only untrained-seed controls).
Entire version: no mapping, stitching or relative-representation evaluation.
Circuits, SAE features, attention heads; recurrence of features distributed across neurons.
Alternative similarity metrics (e.g. CKA, kNN) and genuinely out-of-distribution inputs.
Whether shared training data causes the recurrence (no data-varying experiment).

missing.what: Token-count ablation (10^3–10^8 tokens): the matched set stabilizes as the token budget grows; count and Jaccard overlap with the previous scale are reported.
Image-count ablation (1–50,000 images): the count plateaus and overlap approaches 1 by 50k images.
Per-family-pair fitted exponents and prefactors for the main scaling curves (e.g. 0.68, 0.54, 0.57, 0.60, 0.49, 0.63, 0.69).
Depth-wise distribution of Rosetta Neurons, used as a non-degeneracy check.

record.verdict_notes: Rows r5–r8 are pipeline-validity controls and were unlinked; the reader's V5 limits_scope and V6 supports labels based on them were dropped. The V5 challenge from DINOv3 was dropped because DINOv3 still has recurring neurons, only without a scaling trend. For V6 (a challenge version), robustness of the exponent to k counts against it; the real-versus-generated image test shows only modest dependence. The measure is single-neuron matching, so the study speaks to neuron-level universality, not global representational geometry. The study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Tests growth in the number of matching MLP neurons with model size, not distance geometry across all data points, performance/capability scaling, or whether all representations align.
No vision-language image-caption pairing or comparison of vision and language models.
Does not test same-architecture models trained from different initializations as a seed comparison.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired alignment evaluation.
Tests recurring MLP neurons and population-level selectivity proxies; does not test recurring circuits, SAE features, or a comprehensive inventory of interpretable features.
Varies mutual top-k and some input distributions/alignment conditions. Does not compare alternative similarity metrics or test out-of-distribution inputs as such.

Finds sublinear growth, a shrinking fraction of matched neurons, and a DINOv3 exception. It does not establish that shared data or objectives cause convergence, and does not show a plateau in the main model families.

tranche.reason: Tests cross-model recurrence and its scaling using neuron-level Pearson matching rather than whole-representation geometric similarity.

source_check.notes: Rosetta matches cover MLP neuron correspondences, not all shared representations or computation. Selectivity measures are proxies; the authors' capacity-allocation account and DINOv3 explanation do not establish training-data or objective causality.

statements.correction: Absolute Rosetta-neuron counts increase sublinearly over the tested language and vision ranges, summarized as up to 30B and 5B parameters; matched fractions shrink; overall alignment asymptotes are untested.
statements.problem: Finite-range growth of absolute neuron counts does not qualify V7's optional plateau or establish the trajectory of overall alignment.
